name: @olai/kolu-client
//: HOW OLAI REACHES KOLU — see src/index.ts, which argues the whole boundary. What this manifest is FOR is the wall: a package cannot depend back on @olai/server, so the direction is physics rather than discipline.
//dependencies: @olai/surface is GONE from these dependencies, and that is the sixth sitting's result rather than an omission: the wire vocabulary this package produces moved INTO it (src/wire), so `@olai/surface` now depends on this package and spreads the slice into its own spec. This package names no olai package at all — the direction is a DAG the manifests enforce (olai-plugin-kolu → kolu-client → nothing). @olai/format is deliberately absent for the same reason it always was: the walk over the vault belongs to whoever holds the vault (@olai/server's claimants.ts), and it is INJECTED (KoluDeps.claimants) rather than imported — the interfaces are parametric in the node type, so a compiler checks that this package cannot read a vault node. The @kolu/* it imports — padi-client, solid-dockrow, surface, surface-daemon, surface-daemon-supervisor, terminal-vocab, detect — are hydrated as raw TypeScript from the Nix store rather than installed from bun.lock, so they are declared once for the whole tree in the root package.json. scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh keeps those versions honest, and packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts confines them: its tenancy claim DERIVES which packages may name the product tier from the plugin registry rather than carrying a list, and the answer for kolu is this package and olai-plugin-kolu, with zero exceptions. (It was check-kolu-deps.sh's fourth assertion, over packages/*/src, allowing this package and @olai/kolu-ui — both that script and that package are gone.) Its fifth keeps ./wire pure — no solid-js, no padi, no format — because @olai/surface spreads that entry and every listener pulls it in statically.
